To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

liver impairment at 1 year post-transplantation was associated with increased mortality and that liver function should therefore be closely monitored after HSCT, particularly in patients with a high risk of liver involvement.
liver affection is common at 1-year after HSCT in adults, but not in children.
liver parameters were elevated in a substantial number of children and young adults undergoing myeloablation and that elevated liver parameters were associated with reduced long-term survival.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether liver involvement after HSCT has an impact on long-term survival.
the question of whether a mild to moderate liver affection at 10-month follow-up is a risk factor for poor outcome in the long-term course of patients undergoing myeloablating HSCT.
the prognostic significance of the liver parameters at 10 months after HSCT in patients who have survived at least 1 year.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the liver parameters at 10 years after allogeneic HSCT in adults and children are not associated with long-term outcome, but the liver parameters at one year after allogeneIC HSCT in adults are associated with long-term outcomes.
there is no significant impact of liver affection on long-term outcome after HSCT.
the presence of liver dysfunction at 1 year after HSCT has a significant negative impact on overall and disease-free survival in the long-term follow-up.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

liver affection at 12 months post HSCT is associated with a poor prognosis in patients who survive the first year after transplantation, and this is especially true for patients who have undergone a T-cell depleted transplant.
the liver function at the time of 1-year followup after HSCT is an independent prognostic factor for survival beyond 1-year follow up.
liver parameters at 10 years after transplantation were significantly associated with survival in patients undergoing HSCT.
The main takeaway from our work is that
1-year liver parameters have a prognostic significance in children and adults after HSCT.

liver involvement is common at long-term follow up, and that the presence of abnormal liver parameters at 12-month follow-up is associated with a higher risk of non-relapse mortality (NRM) and overall mortality.
the liver parameters at 12 months after HSCT are predictive of long-term survival.
